# waroom_service_runbook_rule (Resource)

Manages a Waroom service runbook rule. A runbook rule links a runbook to the incidents of a service whose title or description matches a regular expression.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Link the /api-server/recovery runbook to incidents of my-service whose title mentions a database outage
resource "waroom_service_runbook_rule" "example" {
  service_name      = "my-service"
  pattern           = "(?i)database.*down"
  target            = "title" # "title" or "description"
  priority          = 10      # lower value = higher priority
  runbook_namespace = "/api-server/recovery"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `pattern` (String) The regular expression matched against the incident title or description (see `target`). It is evaluated by Waroom (Ruby regular expression syntax), which rejects an invalid expression.
- `priority` (Number) The priority of the rule. A lower value means a higher priority. Must be 0 or greater.
- `runbook_namespace` (String) The namespace of the runbook to link, with the leading slash (e.g. `/default`, `/api-server/recovery`). The runbook must exist.
- `service_name` (String) The name of the Waroom service to which the runbook rule belongs. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `target` (String) What `pattern` is matched against: `title` or `description` of the incident.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) The time the runbook rule was created, in RFC 3339 format.
- `id` (String) Runbook rule ID. This is an alias for `uuid`.
- `updated_at` (String) The time the runbook rule was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.
- `uuid` (String) The unique identifier (UUID) of the runbook rule. This is automatically generated by Waroom.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Service runbook rules can be imported by specifying the service name and rule UUID separated by a comma
# Format: service_name,uuid
import {
  to = waroom_service_runbook_rule.example
  id = "my-service,123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Service runbook rules can be imported by specifying the service name and rule UUID separated by a comma
# Format: service_name,uuid
terraform import waroom_service_runbook_rule.example my-service,123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
```
